ai.literal: Without examining, than making friendship, ruin there is none; having established friendship after, abandonment there is none, to those who cherish friendship.
ai.translation: There is no greater ruin than contracting a friendship without prior examination; for once a bond is formed, those who truly cherish friendship cannot abandon it.
ai.modern: ஆராயாமல் நட்புக்கொள்வதை விடப் பெரிய கேடு வேறு இல்லை; நட்புக்கொண்ட பிறகு, நட்பைப் பேணிக் காப்பவர்களுக்கு அதைக் கைவிடுதல் என்பது இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the danger of entering into friendships hastily. The word 'nāṭātu' means acting without careful examination or inquiry. The poet warns that there is no worse ruin than making a friend without testing their character first, because for those who truly value and practice friendship ('naṭpu āḷpavarkku'), abandoning a friend ('vīṭu') later is simply not an option. Therefore, the choice must be made with utmost care before the bond is sealed.

ai.literal: Having examined and examined, he who does not accept friendship, in the end, to himself, dying grief will give.
ai.translation: The friendship formed by one who does not repeatedly and thoroughly examine a person beforehand will, in the end, bring him grief that is fatal.
ai.modern: மீண்டும் மீண்டும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து ஒருவருடன் நட்புக்கொள்ளாதவனுடைய நட்பு, இறுதியில் அவனுக்குச் சாகுமளவிற்குத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the critical importance of thoroughly testing a person's character before befriending them. The repetition of the word 'ayntu' (having examined) highlights that scrutiny must be continuous and rigorous, not a casual or one-time affair. If one enters into a friendship blindly without such careful investigation, that relationship will eventually bring immense, life-threatening sorrow. The word 'kaṭaimuṟai' indicates the ultimate, inevitable outcome of such carelessness, while 'cām tuyaram' vividly describes a grief so intense that it feels like death itself.

ai.literal: Character and, lineage and, faults and, undiminishing associates and, having known, bind friendship.
ai.translation: Examine a person's character, lineage, faults, and the character of their undiminishing associates, and only then secure their friendship.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய குணத்தையும், குடும்பப் பின்னணியையும், குற்றங்களையும், குறையாத நல்ல சுற்றத்தாரையும் ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து அவரோடு நட்புக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential criteria for choosing a friend. Before forming a bond of friendship, one must thoroughly examine four aspects of a person: their personal character (குணம்), their family background or lineage (குடிமை), their inherent flaws or faults (குற்றம்), and the quality of their constant associates (குன்றா இனம்). The word 'யாக்க' literally means 'to bind' or 'to tie', emphasizing that friendship should be a strong, deliberate bond formed only after careful investigation ('அறிந்து'). By evaluating these aspects, one avoids the pitfalls of making alliances with unsuitable companions.

ai.literal: Having been born in a noble family, him who is ashamed of blame in himself, even by giving, securing friendship is necessary.
ai.translation: One must secure the friendship of a person born of noble lineage who shrinks from disgrace, even if one has to give up something of value to obtain it.
ai.modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து, தன் மேல் பழி வருவதற்கு நாணுகின்ற ஒருவனுடைய நட்பை, ஏதேனும் கொடுத்தாவது நாம் பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential qualities of an ideal friend and the lengths to which one should go to secure their companionship. The poet identifies two key traits: being born into a family of good values (குடிப்பிறந்து) and possessing a deep-seated dread of disgrace or wrongdoing (பழிநாணுவான்). A person who fears blame will naturally act with integrity and loyalty. The phrase 'கொடுத்தும் கொளல்வேண்டும்' emphasizes that such a virtuous friend is so rare and valuable that one should be willing to sacrifice material wealth or other resources just to win their friendship.

ai.literal: Speaking so as to make one weep, reproving wrongdoing, and making the right path known—the friendship of those who are capable of this, having examined, acquire.
ai.translation: One should carefully examine and secure the friendship of those who are capable of speaking frankly to make one weep for one's faults, reproving wrongdoing, and guiding one to the right path.
ai.modern: தவறு செய்யும்போது அழும்படி எடுத்துச் சொல்லி, தீமையைக் கண்டித்து, நல்வழியை அறியச் செய்ய வல்லவர்களின் நட்பை ஆராய்ந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential qualities of a true friend who is worth seeking out. A genuine friend does not merely flatter; they have the courage to speak painful truths to correct our mistakes, even if it makes us weep. They actively reprove us when we stray into wrongdoing and guide us back to the path of virtue. The poet advises us to carefully examine and secure the friendship of such capable individuals who can act as our moral guides.

ai.literal: Even in adversity, is there a benefit? It is a rod that extends and measures one's friends.
ai.translation: Is there any benefit to be found even in adversity? Yes, it is a measuring rod that extends to gauge the true worth of one's friends.
ai.modern: துன்பத்திலும் ஒரு நன்மை உண்டோ? தன் நண்பர்களை நீட்டி அளந்து பார்க்கும் ஒரு அளவுகோல் அது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that even misfortune or ruin (கேடு) has a positive side. It acts as a measuring rod (கோல்) to test and evaluate the true character of one's friends and relatives (கிளைஞர்). When we are in trouble, we can easily see who stands by us and who abandons us. Thus, adversity serves as a practical tool to measure the depth and sincerity of our relationships.

ai.literal: The profit that is to a person is the friendship of fools having shunned and completely abandoning.
ai.translation: The greatest profit a person can acquire is to completely shun and abandon the friendship of fools.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்குக் கிடைக்கும் மிகப்பெரிய இலாபம் என்பது, அறிவில்லாதவர்களின் நட்பை முற்றிலும் விலக்கி விட்டுவிடுவதுதான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that gain is not always about acquiring something new; sometimes, the greatest gain is letting go of what is harmful. The poet defines 'profit' (ஊதியம்) for an individual as the act of completely abandoning (விடல்) and shunning (ஒரீஇ) the friendship (கேண்மை) of foolish or ignorant people (பேதையார்). The word 'ஒரீஇ' is a poetic form that emphasizes the absolute necessity of distancing oneself from such toxic associations. By framing this avoidance as a positive 'profit', the couplet highlights how destructive foolish companions can be to one's life.

ai.literal: Do not think of things that diminish the mind; do not accept the friendship of those who, in times of distress, cut off the path of support.
ai.translation: Never harbor thoughts that diminish the greatness of your mind; likewise, never accept the friendship of those who abandon you in times of distress.
ai.modern: மனம் தளரக்கூடிய எண்ணங்களை நினைக்க வேண்டாம்; துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் வழியைக் கைவிட்டு விலகிப் போகிறவர்களின் நட்பைக் கொள்ள வேண்டாம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises the learner on two crucial things to avoid for maintaining personal dignity and strength. First, one must never think of thoughts that weaken or diminish the resolve and greatness of the mind (உள்ளம் சிறுகுவ உள்ளற்க). Second, one must never accept the friendship of those who cut off support (ஆற்றறுப்பார்) and leave one stranded in times of distress (அல்லற்கண்). Here, 'ஆற்று' refers to the path of support or strength, and 'அறுப்பார்' refers to those who sever that connection when it is needed most. True strength lies in keeping the mind elevated and avoiding fair-weather friends.

ai.literal: At the time of ruin, the friendship of those who abandon, at the time of death, even if thought of, the mind will burn.
ai.translation: The friendship of those who abandon you in times of ruin will burn your mind, even if you think of it at the moment of death.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் கைவிட்டு விலகிப் போகின்றவர்களின் நட்பு, ஒருவருக்கு இறுதி காலம் நெருங்கும் போது நினைத்துப் பார்த்தாலும் மனதைச் சுட்டு வருத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the lingering pain caused by fair-weather friends. The poet states that the friendship of those who abandon us when we fall into ruin (keṭuṅkālai) is so toxic that even thinking about it on one's deathbed (aṭuṅkālai) will burn the heart. The word 'aṭu' here means to destroy or kill, referring to the final moments of life. The betrayal of a false friend leaves a scar so deep that it hurts even at the very end of one's existence.

ai.literal: Cultivate the friendship of those who are free from blemish; even by giving something, abandon the friendship of those who lack suitability.
ai.translation: Cultivate the friendship of those who are free from faults; even if you must give away something to do so, abandon the friendship of those who are unsuitable.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்றவர்களுடைய நட்பை விரும்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள்; நமக்குத் தகுதி இல்லாதவர்களுடைய நட்பை, ஏதேனும் ஒன்றை அவர்களுக்குக் கொடுத்தாவது கைவிடுங்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises the learner on how to choose and manage relationships. It urges us to seek and embrace the friendship of those who are pure and free from moral blemishes. Conversely, we must distance ourselves from those who lack compatibility or proper character. The poet emphasizes that we should be willing to give up something of value, if necessary, as a price to safely sever ties with unsuitable companions.
